feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: it presents a clear leadership profile, solid progression, and relevant platform/communications expertise. Impact is good, but the document is somewhat dense and repetitive, and it would be stronger with more quantified outcomes and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience align well around digital platform leadership, governance, analytics, and communications systems.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure at one organization with visible progression from coordinator to director to consultant signals trust and growth.  
- Good use of scale indicators: examples like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity: include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption rates, campaign performance, or cost savings.  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; consolidate to improve scannability and avoid repetition.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists is inconsistent; use either “and” or the serial comma consistently (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other entries). No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and foreground the strongest differentiators: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and public-sector scale.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language such as “leading” or “delivering.”
- Consider adding one concrete scale signal from recent roles (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, or 50+ publishers) to increase impact.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers scalable editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is echoed throughout the skills sections and work history.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the headline, topline skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership scope will make it feel more distinctive and executive-level.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and shorten longer items for cleaner scanning.
- Replace “communications operations” with “communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Consider this tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, swap “content discovery” for “user experience” only if AI/search is a priority target role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming either this section or the Topline Skills section to avoid repetition.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already strongly established elsewhere in the CV.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block is dense and repeats several themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and format each item as: project name + one concise impact-focused sentence.
- Replace generic verbs (“Built,” “Developed”) with more specific ones where possible: “Launched,” “Led,” “Created,” “Produced.”
- Tighten wording for clarity: e.g., “vector search and bill-level AI chat” → “vector search with bill-level AI chat”; “modular structure designed for continued campaign growth” → “modular architecture for future campaign expansion.”
- If available, add one measurable detail to 1–2 projects (users, content volume, campaign reach, event audience, etc.).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with Work Experience bullets; keep this block as selected examples, not a restatement.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item here; consider leading with it to reduce repetition.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a results-oriented consulting entry. Tighten it around highest-value contributions and avoid repeating NACo achievements already covered in prior roles and Recent Projects.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + seniority: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web governance, campaign infrastructure, and content operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused lines, e.g.:
- “Built and optimized cross-channel workflows, analytics, and publishing systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Designed Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval approach, structured content design, and user discovery experience.”
- Replace generic phrases like “deliver CMS development” and “advise on best practices” with outcomes, scale, or stakeholders served.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, teams supported, launch dates, efficiency gains, or engagement improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording overlaps with prior NACo entries on governance, analytics, Drupal, and multi-channel operations.
- Microsite and AI search details also duplicate Recent Projects; keep this item higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be stronger if the opening were tighter, bullets started with outcomes, and channel-management points were less repetitive with the adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to emphasize biggest wins first: website migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio build, then governance/operations.
- Add outcome language where possible: e.g., “migrated 10,000+ pages to Drupal for 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ publishers” and quantify reporting efficiency, production savings, or engagement gains.
- Tighten channel bullet: focus on ownership and scale, not generic oversight: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version more strategic and less day-to-day.
- Video/programming language also echoes earlier NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and expanding organizational capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the earlier Digital Media Manager role and the later Director role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing scale-up, coordination, and channel ownership rather than broad digital leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed day-to-day multi-channel communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial planning and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets to outcomes and ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show growth/impact: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is too close to the Director role’s broader channel oversight.
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; here, stress expansion/standardization rather than initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize strategic leadership areas not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, senior-level language: “Enterprise web strategy,” “Editorial governance and publishing operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector and advocacy communications,” “Audience-centered content strategy.”
- Use parallel noun phrases and remove filler like “focused”; “Audience-centered content strategy” is cleaner than “Audience-focused content planning.”
- Consider aligning wording to recent impact areas from 2022–present, e.g. “Enterprise web strategy and modernization” to reflect the 10,000+ page Drupal migration.
- If space allows, make one skill outcome-oriented: “Editorial governance and publishing operations at scale.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also repeats multiple recent role bullets; keep this section concise and non-narrative.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages

- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize highest-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and delivery leadership rather than exhaustive platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, with most relevant platforms first: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Consider dropping lower-signal items unless they are current selling points for target roles: SharePoint, Power Pages, WordPress.
- Replace “technical execution” jargon with clearer impact-oriented language if space allows: “Web platforms, CMS modernization and technical delivery.”
- If you want one proof point, add a light qualifier: “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ page public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly all tools here repeat the “Technical + IT” section; keep this version shorter and more strategic.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid expanding it twice.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” or “Analytics infrastructure, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than separating every platform with broader concepts.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business language: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” instead of “Leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity) - KPI framework development - Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting - SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory below.
- “Performance analysis” may overlap with broader “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and recent NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad nouns with capability-led terms: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera direction,” “Studio buildout and operations.”

- Livestream, hybrid and virtual event delivery
- PTZ camera systems and multi-camera workflows
- Studio buildout and broadcast operations

- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations”; vary phrasing or trim one instance.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” is close to work-experience bullets about studio/event capacity; keep this section skills-focused, not descriptive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show depth/order by relevance: **Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migration, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, group by strength: **Enterprise CMS: Drupal, SharePoint, Power Pages | Publishing platforms: WordPress, GitHub Pages**
- Put **Drupal first and keep it prominent**, since it is the clearest recent platform tied to major impact in 2022–present roles.
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** unless you can point to meaningful professional use; it reads lighter than the others.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or using one section for platforms and the other for implementation skills.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating generic CMS language here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and implementation-focused so it adds depth rather than repeating skills already stated elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rename to emphasize applied capability: “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Automation.”
- Tighten and group related tools: “HTML5/CSS3, JavaScript/jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add level/context to stronger recent tools: e.g., “Cloudflare Workers (serverless scripting), GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation), GTM (tag deployment and event tracking).”
- Consider replacing older/generic items with more current, higher-value phrasing tied to recent work: “front-end implementation,” “technical troubleshooting,” “workflow automation,” or “deployment pipelines.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; keep them in one place or vary the framing.
- GTM may also fit better under Analytics/Optimization unless you specifically used it for implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. Since the CV already emphasizes workflow architecture elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around automation and operational use.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant systems first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of just listing tools, e.g.: **Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana/Trello (project tracking), Slack/Teams/Basecamp (team coordination)**
- Consider trimming lower-value/general tools if space is tight; keep the list focused on platforms that support your recent systems/governance work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating this exact phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is limited, they add less differentiation than Airtable, Power Automate, or Zapier.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this line is too bare to show level of use or strategic value. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/strength in parentheses: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, segmentation, member communications**
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp** if Higher Logic was your primary platform at NACo

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding phrases like “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or “multi-channel communications” here; those are already covered in recent work experience and core competencies.
- Don’t over-describe outcomes in this skills line; measurable email impact belongs in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 NACo entries.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, it should be tighter, more tool-specific, and avoid broad capability terms already evidenced in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing**
- Replace **SEO** with **Google Search Console** or **SEO analysis** to make it more concrete and tool/skill-specific.
- Remove **Dashboarding** since reporting/dashboard creation is already implied by Looker Studio and Power BI.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recently used tools first: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping the broader framing there and making this section strictly tools/platforms.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid adding vague terms here that don’t add new information.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience growth, engagement, or production volume.
- Tighten the close to show supervision without overstating seniority: “Mentored a digital media associate on day-to-day content production and publishing workflows.”
- Possible full version: “Promoted through two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving publishing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while mentoring a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version tactical, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination, and trim broad phrases that are better demonstrated in more recent positions.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around distinct, concrete contributions: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications.”
- Make the standout achievement the lead clause: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Tighten “Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” to something more specific, e.g. “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program outreach and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of episodes, audiences served, project types, or teams/stakeholders supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in later digital/media roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership in multimedia here if later entries show larger-scale video, studio, and platform ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting tools, but this item is currently generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. It should emphasize software/tools only and avoid repeating broader capabilities already proven in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
